items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: obviously on the advice of Philly Joe, Hank Mobley showed up in this house.

ctx.x: Very interesting story — there was a bass player in London called John Hart, who was part of, I believe he was part of the Woolworth family so at that time he was very well off and had a very large house in one of the best parts of London. And Philly Joe Jones came to live with him. It was extraordinary. I mean I think it was because there was access to drugs on the National Health you know. So he could register as an addict and he didn’t have to be hounded by the police or anything like that. But he took up…

got to me and I was panicking. I was going I can’t do a five chorus Coltrane impersonation you know, what am I going to do? Oh, I’ll play one note. I’ll play it again and add another one. Oh I’ll play it again, the third one, and then I’ll invert it — hang on a minute, this is what you do. And at the end of the number he came over to me and he said, “You play like Joe Henderson.” He ignored everybody else and came over — and I thought now I understand improvisation.
